UC metric view eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics (query measures with MEASURE(`<measure name>`) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics):
version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd

comment: "HEDIS GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment) for the diabetes population aged\
  \ 18-75, computed live over the gold evidence base. Denominator = eligible diabetes\
  \ patients. Compliant (Blood Sugar Controlled) = last A1c of the measurement year\
  \ is 9.0% or below. HEDIS indicators over the eligible population: Good Control\
  \ Rate (last A1c < 8.0%) and Poor Control Rate (last A1c > 9.0% OR no A1c test).\
  \ HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below\
      \ (Blood Sugar Controlled); NOT_MET = last A1c above 9.0% or no A1c test. The\
      \ rule lives in this metric view, not in gold."
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'Met' WHEN evidence_datetime IS NULL
      THEN 'No A1c test in measurement year' ELSE 'Last A1c above 9%' END
    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\
      \ Group care gaps by reason."
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-75'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (eligible population is 18-75).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 18-75 eligible for GSD (the measure denominator).
      One row per patient.
    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one A1c test in the measurement year
      (not a HEDIS indicator; testing coverage).
    display_name: Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - tested patients
      - a1c tested
      - patients with an a1c

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value <= 9.0)
    comment: Eligible patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below
      (Blood Sugar Controlled; the measure numerator) — computed live from the evidence.
    display_name: Compliant Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - compliant count
      - patients met
      - blood sugar controlled
      - controlled patients

  - name: GSD Compliance Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Compliant Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible diabetes patients whose last A1c of the measurement
      year is 9.0% or below (Blood Sugar Controlled; the inverse of the HEDIS GSD
      > 9.0% indicator). Re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: GSD Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - gsd rate
      - blood sugar controlled rate
      - met rate

  - name: Good Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value < 8.0)
    comment: Patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is < 8.0% (good glycemic control)
      — band computed live from evidence_value.
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - good control
      - well controlled
      - a1c under 8

  - name: Good Control Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Good Control Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: "HEDIS GSD < 8.0% indicator: share of eligible patients whose last A1c\
      \ of the measurement year is below 8.0%."
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - good control rate
      - a1c under 8 rate

  - name: Poor Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value > 9.0 OR evidence_datetime IS NULL)
    comment: "Patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is above 9.0%, or who\
      \ had no A1c test (HEDIS counts a missing test as > 9.0%)."
    display_name: Poor Control (>9%) Patients
    format:
      type

rows.context:
Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 Last HbA1c of the measurement year ≤ 9.0% (blood sugar controlled) Reported as two rates over all eligible patients: < 8.0% (good control) and > 9.0% (poor control; a missing test counts as > 9.0%). General target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which applies the same two cut-offs to everyone: the
last A1c of the year below 8.0% (good control) or above 9.0% (poor control, where a missing test also counts as
poor). The measure answers *"how controlled is the population?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific
patient's target be?"*.

- Check HbA1c **every 3 months** for patients who are above individualized goal or whose therapy has changed.
- Check HbA1c **every 6 months** for patients who are stable at goal.
- Do not react to a single out-of-range HbA1c; confirm with a repeat before escalating therapy.
The GSD measure reads only the **last** A1c of the measurement year, so it cannot distinguish a patient checked
quarterly from one checked once.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

> Synthetic payer memo for the Care Protocol Context & Ontology demo. HEDIS-aligned, not NCQA-certified, not
> for clinical use. This memo **supersedes** the MY2025 glycemic-status guidance for measurement year 2026.

# GSD Poor-Control Rate by Clinic — MY2026 (through 2026-10-30)

**Overall, 36.6% of eligible patients are in poor control (877 of 2,399).** Rates range from **32.6% (CLINIC-05)** to **39.7% (CLINIC-06)** across all eight clinics. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d3d22ccffb6d4052b7059b8c6955bf11?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_98ef81) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174)

<!-- begin-embedded:query_ae405e -->
| clinic_id | eligible_patients | poor_control_patients | no_a1c_test | a1c_above_9 | poor_control_rate_pct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLINIC-06 | 272 | 108 | 78 | 30 | 39.7 |
| CLINIC-08 | 290 | 111 | 72 | 39 | 38.3 |
| CLINIC-04 | 301 | 114 | 79 | 35 | 37.9 |
| CLINIC-01 | 285 | 106 | 69 | 37 | 37.2 |
| CLINIC-07 | 299 | 109 | 72 | 37 | 36.5 |
| CLINIC-03 | 342 | 122 | 94 | 28 | 35.7 |
| CLINIC-02 | 312 | 110 | 88 | 22 | 35.3 |
| CLINIC-05 | 298 | 97 | 66 | 31 | 32.6 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_ae405e -->

## What drives each clinic's rate

Most poor-control patients had **no A1c test** (618 of 877 overall, \~70%). The remaining 259 had a last A1c above 9%. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d3d22ccffb6d4052b7059b8c6955bf11?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_98ef81)

- **CLINIC-06 (39.7%)** — highest rate. 78 untested + 30 with A1c > 9% out of 272 eligible. The gap is driven primarily by untested patients.
- **CLINIC-08 (38.3%)** — 72 untested + 39 with A1c > 9% out of 290. Has the most patients with a last A1c above 9%, so the problem is more about glycemic control than testing gaps.
- **CLINIC-04 (37.9%)** — 79 untested + 35 with A1c > 9% out of 301.
- **CLINIC-03 (35.7%)** — 94 untested (the most of any clinic) + only 28 with A1c > 9% out of 342. Its problem is overwhelmingly testing gaps.
- **CLINIC-05 (32.6%)** — best performer. 66 untested + 31 with A1c > 9% out of 298. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d3d22ccffb6d4052b7059b8c6955bf11?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_ae405e)

## Scope and definition

- **Poor control** = last A1c of the measurement year is above 9.0%, **or** no A1c test. Denominator is all eligible diabetes patients aged 18–75. Lower is better. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174) [GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/09e5fd5b-c4ed-42a7-bf34-a009c6771444?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **Date cutoff:** the data runs through 2026-10-30; the year isn't over, so some currently-untested patients may still get tested, and rates may improve by year-end. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_gsd?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- This repeats the same analysis from a prior run, re-executed on current data. [GSD poor-control by clinic](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f0c13bffeb4b493296f850afa936eee2?o=7474653847172668)
- This is synthetic demo data, HEDIS-aligned but not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD, and frailty exclusions are not applied, so denominators may run slightly high. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5b26413f-23e8-4fe9-913f-c627f2cb9307)

UC metric view eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics (query measures with MEASURE(`<measure name>`) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics):
version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd

comment: "HEDIS GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment) for the diabetes population aged\
  \ 18-75, computed live over the gold evidence base. Denominator = eligible diabetes\
  \ patients. Compliant (Blood Sugar Controlled) = last A1c of the measurement year\
  \ is 9.0% or below. HEDIS indicators over the eligible population: Good Control\
  \ Rate (last A1c < 8.0%) and Poor Control Rate (last A1c > 9.0% OR no A1c test).\
  \ HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below\
      \ (Blood Sugar Controlled); NOT_MET = last A1c above 9.0% or no A1c test. The\
      \ rule lives in this metric view, not in gold."
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'Met' WHEN evidence_datetime IS NULL
      THEN 'No A1c test in measurement year' ELSE 'Last A1c above 9%' END
    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\
      \ Group care gaps by reason."
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-75'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (eligible population is 18-75).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 18-75 eligible for GSD (the measure denominator).
      One row per patient.
    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one A1c test in the measurement year
      (not a HEDIS indicator; testing coverage).
    display_name: Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - tested patients
      - a1c tested
      - patients with an a1c

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value <= 9.0)
    comment: Eligible patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below
      (Blood Sugar Controlled; the measure numerator) — computed live from the evidence.
    display_name: Compliant Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - compliant count
      - patients met
      - blood sugar controlled
      - controlled patients

  - name: GSD Compliance Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Compliant Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible diabetes patients whose last A1c of the measurement
      year is 9.0% or below (Blood Sugar Controlled; the inverse of the HEDIS GSD
      > 9.0% indicator). Re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: GSD Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - gsd rate
      - blood sugar controlled rate
      - met rate

  - name: Good Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value < 8.0)
    comment: Patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is < 8.0% (good glycemic control)
      — band computed live from evidence_value.
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - good control
      - well controlled
      - a1c under 8

  - name: Good Control Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Good Control Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: "HEDIS GSD < 8.0% indicator: share of eligible patients whose last A1c\
      \ of the measurement year is below 8.0%."
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - good control rate
      - a1c under 8 rate

  - name: Poor Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value > 9.0 OR evidence_datetime IS NULL)
    comment: "Patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is above 9.0%, or who\
      \ had no A1c test (HEDIS counts a missing test as > 9.0%)."
    display_name: Poor Control (>9%) Patients
    format:
      type

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 Last HbA1c of the measurement year ≤ 9.0% (blood sugar controlled) Reported as two rates over all eligible patients: < 8.0% (good control) and > 9.0% (poor control; a missing test counts as > 9.0%). General target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which applies the same two cut-offs to everyone: the
last A1c of the year below 8.0% (good control) or above 9.0% (poor control, where a missing test also counts as
poor). The measure answers *"how controlled is the population?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific
patient's target be?"*.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

- Check HbA1c **every 3 months** for patients who are above individualized goal or whose therapy has changed.
- Check HbA1c **every 6 months** for patients who are stable at goal.
- Do not react to a single out-of-range HbA1c; confirm with a repeat before escalating therapy.
The GSD measure reads only the **last** A1c of the measurement year, so it cannot distinguish a patient checked
quarterly from one checked once.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

## 73 GSD-Eligible Diabetics Aged 65–75 Had A1c Above 9% and No Statin in MY2026

Of the GSD-eligible diabetics aged 65–75 in measurement year 2026, **73 patients** had a last A1c above 9% (through 2026-10-30) **and** no statin dispensed in MY2026 through 2026-10-30. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f9b5bb3b63ed467894e368fbdd3bce4e?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_234e0c) [Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (ect)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01f1d411909b14298252fdf627a2c474?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Definitions Used

- **A1c above 9%**: the patient's last A1c of MY2026 is strictly above 9.0% — the GSD poor-control threshold. A result of exactly 9.0% does not count. Patients with no A1c test are excluded since they have no A1c above 9%. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174) [GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/09e5fd5b-c4ed-42a7-bf34-a009c6771444?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **No statin**: the patient has no statin dispensed in MY2026 in the SPD statin-therapy measure data (through 2026-10-30). Statins are matched from drug ingredients to specific products ordered via RxNorm subsumption. Every GSD patient aged 65–75 also appears in the SPD data, since SPD covers ages 40–75. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-7408a2b2-dea4-490f-ab3c-0f41d8901eca) [SPD — Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c8324591-625b-44db-9f8b-c57e9ba5dd7b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **The 2026-10-30 cutoff**: the data naturally ends near that date — the latest A1c is from 2026-10-30 and the latest statin order is from 2026-10-28, with zero statin orders after the cutoff. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f9b5bb3b63ed467894e368fbdd3bce4e?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b4fbc0)

### Note on the Genie Space Result

The certified Genie space returned **72** rather than 73. The difference is one patient whose A1c was recorded on 2026-10-30 at 07:53 AM (A1c = 11.2%). The Genie's timestamp comparison (`<= '2026-10-30'`) treated the cutoff as midnight, excluding that intra-day record. The corrected SQL includes the full day, yielding **73**. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f9b5bb3b63ed467894e368fbdd3bce4e?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_526a6b)

**Caveat:** This is synthetic data following HEDIS rules but is not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD, frailty, and contraindication exclusions are not applied, so the count may run slightly high. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5b26413f-23e8-4fe9-913f-c627f2cb9307)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` g
JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_spd` s
  ON g.`patient_id` = s.`patient_id`
  AND s.`measurement_year` = 2026
WHERE g.`measurement_year` = 2026
  AND g.`age` BETWEEN 65 AND 75
  AND g.`evidence_datetime` <= '2026-10-30 23:59:59'
  AND g.`evidence_value` > 9.0
  AND (s.`evidence_datetime` IS NULL OR s.`evidence_datetime` > '2026-10-30 23:59:59')

-- Check A1c records on 2026-10-30 with time > 00:00:00 for the relevant population
SELECT g.`patient_id`, g.`evidence_datetime`, g.`evidence_value`
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` g
WHERE g.`measurement_year` = 2026
  AND g.`age` BETWEEN 65 AND 75
  AND g.`evidence_value` > 9.0
  AND CAST(g.`evidence_datetime` AS DATE) = '2026-10-30'
  AND g.`evidence_datetime` > '2026-10-30 00:00:00'
ORDER BY g.`evidence_datetime`

SELECT COUNT(*) AS gsd_not_in_spd
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` g
LEFT JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_spd` s
  ON g.`patient_id` = s.`patient_id` AND s.`measurement_year` = 2026
WHERE g.`measurement_year` = 2026
  AND g.`age` BETWEEN 65 AND 75
  AND s.`patient_id` IS NULL

SELECT 
  (SELECT MAX(`evidence_datetime`) FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026) AS max_a1c_dt,
  (SELECT MAX(`evidence_datetime`) FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_spd` WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026) AS max_statin_dt,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_spd` WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026 AND `evidence_datetime` > '2026-10-30 23:59:59') AS statin_after_cutoff

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. UC metric view eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics (query measures with MEASURE(`<measure name>`) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics):
version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence

comment: "Diabetes care-protocol Step 3 adherence: after an A1c result > 9% (poor\
  \ control), was there a follow-up A1c within 90 days? The process-adherence layer\
  \ that reveals WHICH step slipped. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: "Clinic (site) the patient belongs to. Protocol-step drift is a CLINIC-level\
      \ signal (masked in the global/annual view), so slice by this to find which\
      \ site slipped."
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Adherence Status
    expr: CASE WHEN followup_within_90d THEN 'MET' WHEN window_closed THEN 'NOT_MET'
      ELSE 'OPEN' END
    comment: MET = a follow-up A1c within 90 days of the > 9% result; NOT_MET = the
      90-day window closed with none; OPEN = window still open (year-to-date) and
      no follow-up yet -- still closable.
    display_name: Adherence Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - step status
      - protocol status
      - followed up

  - name: Follow-up Type
    expr: "COALESCE(followup_type, 'none')"
    comment: "What satisfied the step: recheck (a follow-up A1c), or none."
    display_name: Follow-up Type
    synonyms:
      - followup
      - follow up type
      - how followed up

measures:
  - name: Trigger Events
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE window_closed)
    comment: "Closed Step-3 obligations: A1c > 9% results whose 90-day window has\
      \ closed (the denominator). Open windows are excluded -- counting early successes\
      \ but not yet-unknown misses would inflate recent rates."
    display_name: Trigger Events
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - triggers
      - high a1c results
      - obligations
      - denominator

  - name: Followed Up In Time
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE window_closed AND followup_within_90d)
    comment: "Obligations met: a follow-up A1c within 90 days of the > 9% result (the\
      \ numerator)."
    display_name: Followed Up In Time
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - followed up
      - met
      - on time followups
      - numerator

  - name: Protocol Step 3 Adherence Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Followed Up In Time`) / MEASURE(`Trigger Events`)
    comment: Share of closed Step-3 obligations followed up within 90 days. Drops
      when the step drifts.
    display_name: Protocol Step 3 Adherence Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - protocol adherence rate
      - step 3 adherence
      - followup rate
      - adherence rate

  - name: Open Obligations
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE NOT followup_within_90d AND NOT window_closed)
    comment: A1c > 9% results whose 90-day follow-up window is still open and not
      yet met -- the members still closable this year.
    display_name: Open Obligations
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - open
      - pending
      - closable
      - still closable
      - open gaps
      - due follow-ups

  - name: Avg Days To Follow-up
    expr: AVG(followup_days)
    comment: Average days from the high A1c to the recheck/therapy change (among those
      followed up).
    display_name: Avg Days To Follow-up
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - average followup days
      - time to followup
      - days to recheck

rows.context:
A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which applies the same two cut-offs to everyone: the
last A1c of the year below 8.0% (good control) or above 9.0% (poor control, where a missing test also counts as
poor). The measure answers *"how controlled is the population?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific
patient's target be?"*.

These are **measurement** changes. The underlying clinical care protocol (A1c targets, cardiorenal
pharmacotherapy, screening cadence) is unchanged. Updating a measure value set is not the same as updating the
standard of care — the demo deliberately distinguishes the two.

Over-treatment carries real harm. Consider **de-intensifying** glucose-lowering therapy and re-targeting a
higher A1c when a patient is over-controlled relative to their individualized goal — for example an older
adult with chronic kidney disease and a history of hypoglycemia whose A1c is 6.5%.
For adults **aged 65 and older**, prefer drug classes **other than insulin, sulfonylureas, and meglitinides**
to minimize hypoglycemia risk. Age-stratified hypoglycemia-avoidance is absent from the HEDIS measures.

rows.context:
## The care protocol (v2025.1) does not define an A1c target for older adults with moderate comorbidity

The protocol's A1c thresholds are **uniform across all adults** — there is no individualized target based on age or comorbidity level. [Care-protocol rules (drug classes, contraindications, thresholds)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/e210469b-4179-45be-91f3-398359a04af3?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/23e2b454fc9b488a97c8a8b644d5f3d5?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b9f439)

### A1c thresholds the protocol does define

| Rule | Threshold | Protocol Section |
|---|---|---|
| Good glycemic control (GSD) | A1c **< 8%** | CP sec2 |
| Poor glycemic control (GSD) | A1c **> 9%** | CP sec3 |
| Step 3 follow-up trigger | A1c ≥ 9% → recheck within **90 days** | CP sec3 / Step 3 |

These apply identically to every eligible diabetic patient (ages 18–75). [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174)

### What was checked

I reviewed all **29 protocol rules** in the `protocol_edges` knowledge graph. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/protocol_edges?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) The only rule tagged with version identifier "CP-DM-2025.1" (section sec2/sec6) recommends **statins for SPD** — it does not address A1c. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/23e2b454fc9b488a97c8a8b644d5f3d5?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b9f439) No rule references "older adult," "elderly," "comorbidity," or any age-stratified glycemic goal. The glossary pages for A1c and Protocol Step 3 likewise contain no age- or comorbidity-based differentiation. [Protocol Step 3 — A1c recheck within 90 days](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/240387f5-7f44-4dc6-9e12-08e037f2d00d?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [HbA1c (A1c) — Hemoglobin A1c](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/198bc1a7-dbd0-4ab8-a66e-d83cc4e95e59?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Bottom line

The closest answer is **< 8%** (the protocol's general "good control" threshold), but this is not a target set specifically for older patients with moderate comorbidity — it applies to everyone. If your v2025.1 protocol document includes an age/comorbidity-stratified target, that rule has not been loaded into this dataset.

> **Note:** This is a synthetic, HEDIS-aligned demo protocol and is **not** NCQA-certified or intended for clinical use. **No.** There is no record of a diabetic eye exam for patient `0b4f4745-1c22-260c-494b-f91aa1e81cfc` — neither inside the EHR nor from any outside source. The workspace contains no claims, HIE, payer supplemental, or outside-provider tables to check. [Prior EED investigation](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/e663c6c67bed468dab554d372274aa05?o=7474653847172668)

### What the measure shows

For MY2026 (2026-01-01 – 2026-12-31), this 61-year-old patient is **eligible** for EED but has **no evidence** of a diabetic eye exam — `evidence_datetime`, `evidence_code`, and `evidence_exam` are all null. The patient is assigned to **CLINIC-02, PANEL-37**. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/68005bb1501c4d669c3157ed4abc8a48?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_1dd328)

- **All procedures, all years:** Searched the full procedure history (silver_procedure) for any description containing eye, retina, ophthalmology, fundus, optometry, vision, or macula. **Zero matches.** The patient has **699 procedures** on file (2017-04-26 through 2026-09-24), including **113 in 2026** — none is an eye exam. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/68005bb1501c4d669c3157ed4abc8a48?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_592f3b) [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/68005bb1501c4d669c3157ed4abc8a48?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_d6f7e5)

The only tables matching those keywords are terminology hierarchies (ICD-10, RxNorm, MeSH), which are unrelated. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/68005bb1501c4d669c3157ed4abc8a48?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_ce631a)

All data in this workspace comes from a single synthetic EHR feed. EED in this system counts only an EHR procedure with a SNOMED code from the EED_EYE_EXAM value set. Until then, this remains a real gap to address through patient outreach. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-0feb1388-da20-46d3-8655-66bd5e2dcb1e)

UC metric view eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics (query measures with MEASURE(`<measure name>`) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics):
version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd

comment: "HEDIS SPD (Statin Therapy) compliance for the diabetes population aged 40-75.\
  \ Denominator = eligible diabetes patients; numerator = dispensed a statin in the\
  \ measurement year (statins resolved from RxNorm ingredients to clinical drugs via\
  \ subsumption). HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: MET = a statin was dispensed in the measurement year; NOT_MET = no statin
      (care gap).
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met' ELSE 'No statin dispensed
      in measurement year' END
    comment: Why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant. Group
      care gaps by reason.
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 55 THEN '40-54' WHEN age < 65 THEN '55-64' ELSE '65-75'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (SPD eligible population
      is 40-75).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports SPD (Statin Therapy).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 40-75 eligible for SPD (the measure denominator).
      One row per patient.
    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: On Statin Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients dispensed a statin in the measurement year (the numerator).
    display_name: On Statin Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - on statin
      - statin count
      - patients on statin
      - patients met

  - name: SPD Compliance Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`On Statin Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible diabetes patients dispensed a statin in the measurement
      year. Numerator / denominator; re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: SPD Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - adherence rate
      - spd rate
      - statin therapy rate
      - statin rate
      - met rate

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (ect): Statin therapy compliance requires dispensing during the measurement year for eligible diabetic adults, and absent dispensing evidence defines gaps.
SPD, Statin Therapy, covers diabetics aged 40–75 dispensed a statin in the measurement year. Patient-level statin gaps on eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd INCLUDE gold_adherence_spd.evidence_datetime IS NULL. Statin gap count is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_spd.evidence_datetime IS NULL).

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json: SPD measures statin therapy, and every unmet patient is assigned the gap reason that no statin was dispensed.
The business term `SPD` means statin therapy. For `gold_adherence_spd` rows with `status = 'NOT_MET'`, assign the exact gap reason `'No statin dispensed'`. The SPD compliance rate is `AVG(CAST(numerator_flag AS INT))` across all eligible SPD rows; gap counts use only rows satisfying `status = 'NOT_MET'`.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev): Statin therapy compliance counts eligible diabetic adults with statin dispensing evidence during the measurement year among all eligible patients.
SPD means Statin Therapy for diabetics aged 40-75 dispensed a statin in the measurement year. Patient-level clinic/panel compliance on eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd is COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*), with all patient rows in that breakdown as denominator. Care gaps INCLUDE evidence_datetime IS NULL.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics: On-statin patients are eligible diabetes patients with statin evidence recorded during the measurement year.
On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics`, the exposed measure `On Statin Patients` is the SPD numerator: eligible patients for whom a statin was dispensed in the measurement year. Query it as `MEASURE(`On Statin Patients`)`, such as `SELECT MEASURE(`On Statin Patients`) AS on_statin_patients FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`spd_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`. Its definition-time expression over the source is `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)`. The `evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL` condition means recorded statin evidence qualifies the patient; this is an aggregated measure, not a row-level predicate to apply directly to the metrics view.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics: SPD measures statin therapy compliance for diabetes patients aged 40 through 75 during each HEDIS measurement year.
`eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics` is a non-materialized Unity Catalog metrics view for HEDIS SPD (Statin Therapy) compliance. It covers the diabetes population aged 40-75 and reports eligible patients, patients dispensed a statin, and the resulting compliance rate. The view is HEDIS-aligned for demonstration and is explicitly not NCQA-certified. Query its measures with `MEASURE()` rather than treating the view as an ordinary row-level table; dimensions may be used directly and measure queries should include `GROUP BY ALL`.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics: Eligible patients are the SPD denominator, while on-statin patients are the numerator for statin adherence reporting.
On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics`, the exposed measure `Eligible Patients` means diabetes patients aged 40-75 eligible for SPD, with one source row per patient. Query it as `MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)` in an explicit grouped query, for example `SELECT MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`) AS eligible_patients FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`spd_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`. The definition-time expression over the source is `COUNT(1)`. This is the denominator; it should be interpreted together with the separate numerator measure `On Statin Patients`, rather than as a count of all patients in an unrelated population.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics: Care-gap reason labels compliant patients as met and identifies noncompliant patients as lacking statin dispensing during the measurement year.
The exposed dimension `Gap Reason` on `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.spd_compliance_metrics` is definition-time derived as `CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met' ELSE 'No statin dispensed in measurement year' END`. The complete listed values are `'Met'` and `'No statin dispensed in measurement year'`. Use `` `Gap Reason` `` to group care gaps by reason; it is a dimension and should be queried directly, while the related `Compliance Status` dimension uses uppercase status codes `'MET'` and `'NOT_MET'`.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (ect).lvdash.json: Care-gap analysis includes only eligible records marked not met, assigning one standardized reason to each measure-specific gap.
Care-gap counts and worklists include only rows where `status='NOT_MET'` in each measure-specific table. The complete reason mapping is: GSD → `'No A1c test in year'`; BPD → `'BP not controlled / no reading'`; SPD → `'No statin dispensed'`; and EED → `'No diabetic eye exam'`. KED uses the flags to distinguish reasons: `CASE WHEN NOT egfr_flag AND NOT uacr_flag THEN 'No eGFR and no uACR' WHEN NOT uacr_flag THEN 'No uACR test' ELSE 'No eGFR test' END`. These conditions are applied before grouping by `measure, gap_reason` and counting patients.

query.sql:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT subject, predicate, object
  FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph
),
eligible AS (
  SELECT subject AS patient
  FROM t
  WHERE predicate = 'eligibleFor'
    AND object = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/Measure/GSD'
),
clinic AS (
  SELECT subject AS patient, object AS clinic
  FROM t
  WHERE predicate = 'attributedTo'
),
obs AS (
  SELECT subject AS patient, object AS obs
  FROM t
  WHERE predicate = 'hasObservation'
),
a1c_tests AS (
  SELECT object AS labtest
  FROM t
  WHERE predicate = 'containsTest'
    AND subject = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/ValueSet/GSD_A1C_TEST'
),
a1c_obs AS (
  SELECT o.patient, o.obs
  FROM obs o
  JOIN t ot ON ot.subject = o.obs AND ot.predicate = 'ofTest'
  JOIN a1c_tests at ON at.labtest = ot.object
),
a1c_values AS (
  SELECT a.patient,
         a.obs,
         try_cast(rd.object AS TIMESTAMP) AS result_dt,
         try_cast(rv.object AS DOUBLE) AS result_val
  FROM a1c_obs a
  JOIN t rd ON rd.subject = a.obs AND rd.predicate = 'resultDateTime'
  JOIN t rv ON rv.subject = a.obs AND rv.predicate = 'resultValue'
),
my2026 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM a1c_values
  WHERE result_dt >= TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND result_dt <= TIMESTAMP '2026-10-30 23:59:59'
),
last_a1c AS (
  SELECT patient,
         result_val,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY patient ORDER BY result_dt DESC) AS rn
  FROM my2026
)
SELECT
  c.clinic,
  COUNT(DISTINCT e.patient) AS eligible_patients,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN la.result_val IS NULL OR la.result_val > 9 THEN e.patient END) AS poor_control_patients,
  ROUND(
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN la.result_val IS NULL OR la.result_val > 9 THEN e.patient END) * 100.0
      / COUNT(DISTINCT e.patient), 2
  ) AS poor_control_rate_pct
FROM eligible e
JOIN clinic c ON c.patient = e.patient
LEFT JOIN last_a1c la ON la.patient = e.patient AND la.rn = 1
GROUP BY c.clinic
ORDER BY c.clinic

query.sql:
WITH patient AS (
  SELECT 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/Patient/00040be9-7fcf-0ca1-0263-b4197b8f8d28' AS pid
),
statin_meds AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t1.subject AS med
  FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph t1
  JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph t2
    ON t1.object = t2.subject
   AND t1.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasIngredient'
   AND t2.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/inDrugClass'
   AND t2.object = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/DrugClass/DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
),
patient_orders AS (
  SELECT o.subject AS order_id, o.object AS med
  FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph po
  JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph o
    ON po.object = o.subject
   AND po.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasMedicationOrder'
   AND o.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/ordersMedication'
  WHERE po.subject = (SELECT pid FROM patient)
)
SELECT
  po.order_id,
  po.med,
  start_t.object AS start_dt,
  stop_t.object AS stop_dt,
  CASE WHEN try_cast(stop_t.object AS TIMESTAMP) IS NULL
         OR try_cast(stop_t.object AS TIMESTAMP) > TIMESTAMP('2026-10-30 00:00:00')
       THEN true ELSE false END AS active_as_of_period_end
FROM patient_orders po
LEFT JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph start_t
  ON start_t.subject = po.order_id
 AND start_t.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/startDateTime'
LEFT JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v8_graph stop_t
  ON stop_t.subject = po.order_id
 AND stop_t.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/stopDateTime'
WHERE po.med IN (SELECT med FROM statin_meds)
ORDER BY try_cast(start_t.object AS TIMESTAMP) DESC

version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_lab_result

comment: "LOINC lab-result measures over the synthetic observation stream, enriched\
  \ with LOINC multiaxial Parts. Group by Lab Concept (Component) to count labs by\
  \ WHAT was measured regardless of code vintage or method -- the multiaxial-identity\
  \ capability a flat code list or a single is-a closure cannot express. Averages\
  \ are only meaningful within a single Concept/Code (units differ across analytes).\
  \ Synthetic; LOINC (c) Regenstrief under the LOINC License."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: Calendar year of the lab result (YEAR(result_ts)).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - result year
      - reporting year

  - name: Lab Concept
    expr: "COALESCE(component, 'Uncoded (no LOINC Part)')"
    comment: "LOINC Component Part -- WHAT the test measures (e.g. 'Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total',\
      \ 'Glomerular filtration rate.predicted', 'Albumin/Creatinine'). The multiaxial\
      \ grouping key: one Concept spans every code/method that measures it. 'Uncoded'\
      \ when the LOINC code has no Part in the demo subset."
    display_name: Lab Concept (LOINC Component)
    synonyms:
      - concept
      - component
      - analyte
      - what was measured
      - lab type
      - loinc component

  - name: LOINC Code
    expr: loinc_code
    comment: "The specific LOINC code of the result (e.g. 4548-4, 17856-6, 98979-8).\
      \ Several codes can share one Lab Concept."
    display_name: LOINC Code
    synonyms:
      - loinc
      - code
      - test code
      - lab code

  - name: Lab Test
    expr: description
    comment: Human-readable lab/test name as recorded on the observation.
    display_name: Lab Test
    synonyms:
      - test name
      - lab name
      - test

  - name: Specimen System
    expr: "COALESCE(specimen_system, 'Unspecified')"
    comment: "LOINC System Part -- the specimen/site (e.g. Blood, Serum or Plasma,\
      \ Urine, Arterial system)."
    display_name: Specimen System
    synonyms:
      - system
      - specimen
      - sample
      - source
      - matrix

  - name: Method
    expr: "COALESCE(method, 'Unspecified')"
    comment: "LOINC Method Part -- the assay/technique (e.g. HPLC, IFCC, MDRD, CKD-EPI).\
      \ Distinguishing Concept from Method is the point: HbA1c by HPLC and by IFCC\
      \ are the SAME Concept, different Method."
    display_name: Method
    synonyms:
      - assay
      - technique
      - measurement method
      - how measured

  - name: Units
    expr: "COALESCE(units, 'Unspecified')"
    comment: Result units of measure as recorded.
    display_name: Units
    synonyms:
      - unit
      - uom
      - units of measure

measures:
  - name: Observations
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Number of lab result rows (one per recorded numeric observation).
    display_name: Observations
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - results
      - result count
      - tests performed
      - number of labs
      - observation count

  - name: Patients Tested
    expr: COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id)
    comment: Distinct patients with at least one result in the grouping. Use this
      (not Observations) for 'how many patients were tested'.
    display_name: Patients Tested
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - patients
      - distinct patients
      - patients with a result
      - tested patients
      - people tested

  - name: Average Result
    expr: AVG(value_num)
    comment: Mean numeric result value. Only meaningful grouped by a single Lab Concept
      or LOINC Code -- units differ across analytes (A1c % vs eGFR mL/min vs mmHg).
    display_name: Average Result
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 2
    synonyms:
      - avg value
      - mean result
      - average value
      - mean

  - name: Min Result
    expr: MIN(value_num)
    comment: Minimum numeric result value in the grouping (interpret within one Concept/Code).
    display_name: Min Result
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 2
    synonyms:
      - minimum
      - lowest
      - min value

  - name: Max Result

    comment: Maximum numeric result value in the grouping (interpret within one Concept/Code).
    display_name: Max Result
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 2
    synonyms:
      - maximum
      - highest
      - max value

rows.context:
For **MY2026**, the eGFR value set is modernized to the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 estimating equation and
**drops the legacy race-based (MDRD) eGFR code** (LOINC 33914-3) that older lab feeds still emit. The MY2026 eGFR
value set is LOINC 98979-8 (CKD-EPI 2021) only. Health systems whose result
feed still carries the legacy code will see eGFR coverage — and therefore KED compliance — fall on otherwise
unchanged data until mapping is updated. This is the second controlled drift scenario in the demo.

Assessment Codes Frequency HbA1c LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" Every 3 months if uncontrolled (> 9%); every 6 months if at goal Kidney (eGFR + uACR) eGFR + uACR LOINC At least annually (KED) Blood pressure LOINC 8480-6 / 8462-4 Every clinical encounter Dilated retinal eye exam Retinal exam procedure Annually; biennially if a prior exam was normal and risk is low

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 Last HbA1c of the measurement year ≤ 9.0% (blood sugar controlled) Reported as two rates over all eligible patients: < 8.0% (good control) and > 9.0% (poor control; a missing test counts as > 9.0%). General target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

CP-GLY-1. Target HbA1c is < 7.0% for most adults. A1c between 8.0% and 9.0% warrants therapy review; A1c > 9.0% is classified poorly controlled and triggers escalation within 3 months. CP-GLY-2. Metformin is first-line glucose-lowering therapy. Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m²; use with caution and do not initiate at eGFR 30–45. CP-GLY-3. For patients with established CKD (eGFR ≥ 20) or heart failure, add an SGLT2 inhibitor regardless of A1c, for organ protection.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from Care Protocol — LOINC Lab Measures (ect): eGFR results include raw LOINC codes linked to component part LP-EGFR through the terminology table.
To include eGFR results in `gold_lab_result`, use `gold_lab_result.loinc_code IN (SELECT loinc_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts WHERE predicate = 'has_component' AND part = 'LP-EGFR')`. The filter direction is INCLUDE, with the complete component value `'LP-EGFR'` and predicate `'has_component'`. The agent's sample question for which codes count as eGFR uses the same predicate and part values.

Inferred snippet (text) from [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev): Cross-year kidney evaluation comparisons can show an artificial decrease when later-year kidney test value sets retain only CKD-EPI evidence.
A later measurement year's KED eGFR value set keeps only the CKD-EPI code. Cross-year KED comparisons can consequently show an artificial drop. The content provides no literal LOINC code or specific later year for this caveat.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics: KED compliance measures kidney-health testing for eligible diabetes patients aged 18 through 85 during each measurement year.
`eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics` is a HEDIS-aligned demonstration metrics view for Kidney Health Evaluation (KED), not an NCQA-certified measure. Its denominator is eligible diabetes patients aged 18-85, and full compliance requires BOTH an eGFR test and a uACR test in the measurement year. Query measures from the metrics view with `MEASURE()` and `GROUP BY ALL`; do not treat the view as an ordinary row-level table or reconstruct its measures with `SUM`/`COUNT`.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from Care Protocol — LOINC Lab Measures (ect): eGFR method breakdown compares observation and patient volume for the glomerular filtration rate predicted concept.
For eGFR results by assay, use `SELECT `Method`, MEASURE(`Observations`) AS results, MEASURE(`Patients Tested`) AS patients FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.lab_result_metrics WHERE `Lab Concept` = 'Glomerular filtration rate.predicted' GROUP BY `Method` ORDER BY results DESC`. The output grain is one row per `Method` within the exact concept `'Glomerular filtration rate.predicted'`. It reports both result observations and distinct patients, ordered by observations descending.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev): Kidney evaluation performance includes both kidney testing components, with urine albumin testing usually identified as the limiting component.
KED means kidney evaluation with eGFR and uACR components. Annual performance from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics groups by `Measurement Year` and selects MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`), MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`), MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`), and MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`). INCLUDE only `Measurement Year` = (SELECT MAX(measurement_year) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked). Explanations show both component rates because uACR is usually limiting. The clinic sample uses the same year filter, groups by Clinic, selects MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`) and MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`), and orders by Clinic.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from Care Protocol — Cohort & Terminology (ect): eGFR laboratory codes share the designated component, and their assay methods come from method Parts attached to those codes.
In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts, INCLUDE predicate = 'has_component' AND part = 'LP-EGFR' to find eGFR codes here. The verified code-set output is concat_ws(',', sort_array(collect_set(loinc_code))) over that selection. For assay methods, return loinc_code, part_name AS method from the same table WHERE predicate = 'has_method' AND loinc_code IN (SELECT loinc_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts WHERE predicate = 'has_component' AND part = 'LP-EGFR'), ordered by loinc_code.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics: eGFR tested patients count eligible people with at least one eGFR test during the measurement year.
On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics`, `eGFR Tested Patients` counts eligible patients with a non-null eGFR test date; its definition-time expression is `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL)`. Query the predefined measure as `MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`)` with `GROUP BY ALL`, for example: `SELECT `Measurement Year`, MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) AS `egfr_tested_patients` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`ked_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`. This is the eGFR component count, not the full KED numerator.

## eGFR in the Care Protocol: Measures, MY2026 Codes, and Where It's Defined

**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation) is the only quality measure that uses eGFR.** For MY2026, a single LOINC code counts: **`98979-8`** (CKD-EPI 2021). Two care-protocol medication rules also reference eGFR thresholds, but they are contraindication rules, not quality measures. [Prior eGFR analysis](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668)

### Where eGFR Is Used

| Context | How eGFR is used | Protocol source |
|---|---|---|
| **KED** (diabetes patients, ages 18–85) | One of two required numerator tests — a patient needs both an eGFR *and* a uACR test in the measurement year | `CP sec5`: `KED monitoredBy LP-EGFR` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-8e0e87c6-ec71-4cc4-bc5a-cfd3232063ea) |
| **SGLT2 inhibitors** | Contraindicated when eGFR < 20 | `CP sec4`: `DRUGCLASS-SGLT2 contraindicatedWhen eGFR_LT_20` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) |
| **Biguanides (Metformin)** | Contraindicated when eGFR < 30 | `CP-GLY-2`: `DRUGCLASS-BIGUANIDE contraindicatedWhen eGFR_LT_30` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) |

GSD, SPD, BPD, EED, and MAD do **not** use eGFR.

### LOINC Codes That Count as eGFR, by Measurement Year

<!-- begin-embedded:query_78f627 -->
| value_set_version | segment_name | egfr_loinc_codes | code_count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2025 | Kidney eval - eGFR (KED) | 33914-3, 98979-8 | 2 |
| 2026 | Kidney eval - eGFR (KED) [MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only] | 98979-8 | 1 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_78f627 -->

- **MY2025**: two codes — `33914-3` (MDRD) and `98979-8` (CKD-EPI)
- **MY2026**: one code — `98979-8` (CKD-EPI only) — the segment name explicitly says *"MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only"* [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_78f627)

### Where It's Defined

1. **Code list** — the `KED_EGFR` segment in the value-set table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/value_set_segment?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668). Each row is tied to a `measurement_year`, so the MY2026 row carries only `98979-8`. You match lab results on `loinc_code = code` for the segment and year you want. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-edda8620-a170-4029-82f4-21a22de79a49) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-c5a7f603-0689-491a-9666-2c038996db63)
2. **Measure logic & thresholds** — the protocol-edges table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/protocol_edges?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668), which records the `monitoredBy` and `contraindicatedWhen` relationships shown above.
3. **Glossary page** — *eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)* [eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/150dfd59-85b9-4efd-8014-bb170bfe626e?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) — lists both LOINC codes and identifies eGFR as one of KED's two tests. Note: this page has **not** been updated for MY2026 and still lists `33914-3`.

### Caveat on the MY2026 Change

Dropping `33914-3` (MDRD) from the MY2026 value set could theoretically lower KED rates if the lab data still uses that code. However, in this synthetic dataset, all lab results from 2023 onward already use `98979-8` (CKD-EPI), so the change has no practical impact on MY2025 or MY2026 KED. It would only matter for historical lookbacks to 2022 or earlier. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-ed62bbb6-6537-45d5-9de2-05957f4f1f00)

UC metric view eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics (query measures with MEASURE(`<measure name>`) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics):
version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd

comment: "HEDIS GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment) for the diabetes population aged\
  \ 18-75, computed live over the gold evidence base. Denominator = eligible diabetes\
  \ patients. Compliant (Blood Sugar Controlled) = last A1c of the measurement year\
  \ is 9.0% or below. HEDIS indicators over the eligible population: Good Control\
  \ Rate (last A1c < 8.0%) and Poor Control Rate (last A1c > 9.0% OR no A1c test).\
  \ HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below\
      \ (Blood Sugar Controlled); NOT_MET = last A1c above 9.0% or no A1c test. The\
      \ rule lives in this metric view, not in gold."
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'Met' WHEN evidence_datetime IS NULL
      THEN 'No A1c test in measurement year' ELSE 'Last A1c above 9%' END
    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\
      \ Group care gaps by reason."
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-75'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (eligible population is 18-75).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 18-75 eligible for GSD (the measure denominator).
      One row per patient.
    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one A1c test in the measurement year
      (not a HEDIS indicator; testing coverage).
    display_name: Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - tested patients
      - a1c tested
      - patients with an a1c

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value <= 9.0)
    comment: Eligible patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below
      (Blood Sugar Controlled; the measure numerator) — computed live from the evidence.
    display_name: Compliant Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - compliant count
      - patients met
      - blood sugar controlled
      - controlled patients

  - name: GSD Compliance Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Compliant Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible diabetes patients whose last A1c of the measurement
      year is 9.0% or below (Blood Sugar Controlled; the inverse of the HEDIS GSD
      > 9.0% indicator). Re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: GSD Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - gsd rate
      - blood sugar controlled rate
      - met rate

  - name: Good Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value < 8.0)
    comment: Patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is < 8.0% (good glycemic control)
      — band computed live from evidence_value.
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - good control
      - well controlled
      - a1c under 8

  - name: Good Control Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Good Control Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: "HEDIS GSD < 8.0% indicator: share of eligible patients whose last A1c\
      \ of the measurement year is below 8.0%."
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - good control rate
      - a1c under 8 rate

  - name: Poor Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value > 9.0 OR evidence_datetime IS NULL)
    comment: "Patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is above 9.0%, or who\
      \ had no A1c test (HEDIS counts a missing test as > 9.0%)."
    display_name: Poor Control (>9%) Patients
    format:
      type

query.sql:
WITH active_meds AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id, rc.ancestor_code AS drug_class
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med m
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc
    ON rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code
   AND rc.ancestor_code LIKE 'DRUGCLASS-%'
  WHERE m.start_ts <= TIMESTAMP('2026-10-30 23:59:59')
    AND (m.stop_ts IS NULL OR m.stop_ts >= TIMESTAMP('2026-10-30 00:00:00'))
),

condition_hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT am.patient_id, am.drug_class, pe.object AS reason
  FROM active_meds am
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
    ON pe.subject = am.drug_class AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs
    ON vs.segment_id = pe.object
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition c
    ON c.patient_id = am.patient_id
   AND c.icd10_code LIKE concat(vs.code, '%')
   AND c.onset_date <= DATE('2026-10-30')
   AND (c.stop_date IS NULL OR c.stop_date > DATE('2026-10-30'))
),

latest_lab AS (
  SELECT patient_id, loinc_code, MAX_BY(value_num, result_ts) AS value_num
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation
  WHERE result_ts <= TIMESTAMP('2026-10-30 23:59:59')
  GROUP BY patient_id, loinc_code
),

lab_hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT am.patient_id, am.drug_class, e.object AS reason
  FROM active_meds am
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges e
    ON e.subject = am.drug_class AND e.predicate = 'contraindicatedWhen'
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges a
    ON a.subject = e.object AND a.predicate = 'appliesTo'
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts lp
    ON lp.part = a.object AND lp.predicate = 'has_component'
  JOIN latest_lab ll
    ON ll.patient_id = am.patient_id AND ll.loinc_code = lp.loinc_code
  WHERE ll.value_num < CAST(e.value AS DOUBLE)
),

all_hits AS (
  SELECT * FROM condition_hits
  UNION
  SELECT * FROM lab_hits
),

total AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS total_affected_patients
  FROM all_hits
)

SELECT
  ah.drug_class,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ah.patient_id) AS patients_for_drug,
  t.total_affected_patients
FROM all_hits ah
CROSS JOIN total t
GROUP BY ah.drug_class, t.total_affected_patients
ORDER BY ah.drug_class

# 67 Patients With Contraindicated Active Orders on 2026-10-30

On that date, **67 distinct patients** had an active medication order for a drug the care protocol contraindicates — either for a condition active that day or for their last lab result on or before that day. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/1c372ad6f6a443fb95a99197d10d0fbe?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_8d2c80)

## By contraindication rule and drug

### Last lab — eGFR below 30 → Metformin (48 patients)
- **Drug:** 24 HR Metformin hydrochloride 500 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet (biguanide class)
- **Rule:** CP-GLY-2 — metformin is contraindicated when the patient's latest eGFR is below 30. [Care-protocol rules (drug classes, contraindications, thresholds)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/e210469b-4179-45be-91f3-398359a04af3?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- Each patient's most recent eGFR result on or before 2026-10-30 fell below the threshold.

### Active condition — Pregnancy → ACE inhibitor (11 patients)
- **Drug:** Lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet (ACE class)
- **Rule:** CP sec4 — ACE inhibitors are contraindicated with pregnancy (ICD-10 Z34, O00, etc.). [Care-protocol rules (drug classes, contraindications, thresholds)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/e210469b-4179-45be-91f3-398359a04af3?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Active condition — Pregnancy → Statin (9 patients)
- **Drugs:** Simvastatin 10 MG Oral Tablet (7 patients) and Simvastatin 20 MG Oral Tablet (2 patients)
- **Rule:** CP sec4 — statins are contraindicated with pregnancy.
- One patient (f2711bd3) had **both** a lisinopril and a simvastatin order active that day, plus two pregnancy codes (normal pregnancy Z34.90 and tubal pregnancy O00.1), which is why 11 + 9 = 20 condition-flagged patients but only 19 distinct people in the condition branch. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/1c372ad6f6a443fb95a99197d10d0fbe?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_2b3604)

### Rules with zero matches
- **Statins with hepatic disease** (K70, K74): no patients matched.
- **SGLT2 inhibitors with eGFR below 20**: no SGLT2 orders exist in the data.
